headline: Tuesday: Dow +0.85% closed above 50,000, S&P 500 -0.50%, Nasdaq -1.48% as chip stocks gave back Monday's Nvidia surge (Micron -11%, ADI -17%). Health care and retailers led. Consumer confidence jumped. A Dec 9 Fed hike is ~95% priced. PCE and GDP due today; closed Thursday.

sectors.why: No clear sector news. A December 9 Fed hike is about 95% priced and the 10-year yield sits near 4.90%, a mild headwind but not a clear direction.
No specific US telecom news. Communication services rose about 0.8% Tuesday, but long Treasury yields near 5.3% weigh on dividend payers.
A December 9 Fed hike is about 95% priced and the 10-year yield is near 4.90%, keeping mortgage and auto loan costs high for homes, cars and furniture.
Staples rose about 1.7% Tuesday as money left chips for defensive names, but J.M. Smucker slipped after results. No clear month-long driver.
Conference Board consumer confidence jumped to its highest in nearly two years, a plus for spending, but a likely Fed hike limits the upside.
No clear sector news this week. Rates are the main factor and a December hike is already expected.
Chips fell hard Tuesday (Micron -11% on memory demand worries, ADI -17%, Nvidia -6%) and HPE sank 16% on a lower AI server margin outlook. Dell's record quarter is a partial offset.
Energy rose about 1% Tuesday, but forecasters expect oil prices to ease into year end. No clear direction.
Financials rose about 0.8% Tuesday and credit spreads narrowed. A December hike can help bank margins but weighs on borrowing, so no clear direction.
Health care led Tuesday's market, but the gains were in drug makers and devices, not in insurers or hospitals. No clear month-long driver.
Health care was the best sector Tuesday (+2.95%) and Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for about $41 billion in cash, a sign of strong deal appetite. Medtronic fell after a revenue miss.
Mixed: Amentum jumped 20% while Dycom fell 18% Tuesday. No clear sector-wide direction.
No clear news for this group.
No clear sector news; materials rose about 0.5% Tuesday. Rate-hike expectations and a firm dollar are a mild headwind.
No clear sector news. Chemical and packaging names follow rates and demand, and neither moved decisively.
Industrials slipped about 0.5% Tuesday. Deere reports today, which can set the tone for farm and machinery names.
Retailers rallied Tuesday (Abercrombie +20%, Kohl's +19%, Dick's +15%, Dollar Tree +11%) and consumer confidence hit a near two-year high. Urban Outfitters fell after hours.
Workday and Autodesk fell about 4% after hours on their results, and AI names were sold Tuesday, but software held up better than chips. No clear direction.
No clear sector news. Holiday travel week; rates are the main factor.
Utilities edged up about 0.2% Tuesday, but the 30-year Treasury near 5.29% and an expected December hike keep pressure on rate-sensitive dividend stocks.

avoid.HPE: Shares fell about 16% on Tuesday as a lower AI server margin outlook overshadowed its raised forecast; wait for the dust to settle.
